analysis:
Reviewed all eight primary analyses and the available replayed patches against the canonical index and detailed T-041. No independently supported security regression was established. Replay is incomplete (48 of 54 reviewed source units omitted); prior analyses and test expectations do not prove production enforcement.

SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator.swift:119-219 introduces shared reads while retaining exclusive default access, queued-writer priority, lock-protected sole-reader upgrade, cancellation cleanup and continuation resumption outside the lock. These visible controls do not show an exclusion or fairness regression. SSDBlockIndex.swift:137-140 adds locked recency lookup; :288-295 forwards the optional expiry cutoff under the disk-budget lock. SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift:29-39 forwards that cutoff through existing ownership/removal guards. The telemetry test-double signature change adds no production authority.

The combined change affects T-041/A-001/TB-007 authentication, sliding TTL, transient staging memory and availability. Cutoff-aware retirement appears intended to preserve genuinely recent hits rather than raise the 30-minute TTL. No supplied evidence establishes changes to account-salted lookup, encryption, attestation, authorization, billing or plaintext exposure.

Material questions remain: verify SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove atomically rechecks lastAccess and persists recency under exclusive file access and epoch ownership, with nil retaining unconditional budget eviction. Verify SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Read.swift:129/204 shared-read callers require exclusive upgrade for corruption deletion/mtime mutation, reauthenticate outdated receipts, preserve same-ID cancellation ownership and bound/refund concurrent staging reservations. Verify SSDWholeRootMaintainer.swift:119-164 uses the cutoff only for TTL and reconciles surviving mtimes without lock-order deadlock. Tests described across units exercise these contracts but cannot resolve missing implementation evidence. Further review should obtain those changed implementations and reconcile the shared-read staging behavior with T-041's reservation description; absence is a coverage limit, not a finding.
